title: Redwood POC scoping with Silver Lining Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a pilot ingesting patient-facing notes: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO via Okta/SAML, RBAC model, audit log ingestion to their SIEM, workload sizing and benchmark plan. Agreed next steps include sharing security pack, running latency/throughput benchmarks on sample data, and scheduling follow-up demo with live tests.
topics: Security: SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS
header: Date: 2029-07-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Jon Fischer (CTO, Silver Lining Health), Priya Nair (Security Lead), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Ravi Mehta (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we're excited to scope this pilot. quick roll call?
[00:08] Jon (Customer): Jon here, hi. Priya here. Aisha here.
[00:12] Carlos (Redwood SE): Carlos here.
[00:15] Maya: cool, great. want to start with success criteria, like what would you consider a successful pilot?
[00:23] Priya: from security perspective, we need SOC two evidence, ISO cert details, and we need SSO via Okta using SAML. also audit logging must be shipable to our Splunk instance, retention 90 days minimum.
[00:36] Jon: and from product, we need summarization quality to meet our baseline metrics and p95 latency under 350ms for typical requests, and cost per user under threshold.
[00:47] Carlos: got it. quick clarification, when you say p95 350, that's under your baseline load or a single-thread?
[00:53] Jon: baseline simulated load, think 12 to 15 QPS with peaks to 20. average tokens per request about 600, some longer threads up to 2k.
[01:03] Carlos: ok that's helpful. For the bench plan I suggest we run two model variants: a quantized 8-bit version on dedicated infra and a hosted low-latency variant. we'll measure p50/p95 and tokens/sec.
[01:15] Priya: we also need to validate KMS integration for keys, and attestation that data at rest is encrypted. our legal team will want evidence.
[01:24] Maya: yes we can share SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and a KMS integration guide, and for SSO we have an Okta SAML guide.
[01:30] Aisha: quick Q - will audit logs include user-level identifiers and the request prompt payload? we can't send PHI in logs to external systems.
[01:39] Carlos: by default we capture metadata and tracing; we can redact prompt payloads or provide truncated hashes. we also support forwarding structured audit logs to your SIEM with configurable fields.
[01:50] Priya: good, we need to map fields to our SIEM schema. also RBAC: we need at minimum roles for admin, devops, analytics, and restricted for PII viewers.
[02:01] Maya: that aligns with Redwood's RBAC profiles; Carlos can walk through role mappings after.
[02:08] Carlos: yeah I can produce a role matrix, but we'll need your list of personas so we can map permissions to model-level and route-level access.
[02:17] Ravi: timeline wise we're aiming to run pilot in two weeks and have security sign-off in four to six weeks, is that realistic?
[02:25] Maya: two weeks for initial bench is doable if we get sample data and IAM access. security sign-off four to six weeks is typical given review cycles.
[02:32] Jon: sample data - we'll provide de-identified notes and a synthetic set that mirrors token distributions.
[02:37] Carlos: perfect. for sizing note: you said 12-15 QPS, avg 600 tokens, peak concurrency 20. for that we'd recommend starting with a 2-GPU dedicated test or a small hosted burst profile to emulate conditions.
[02:52] Aisha: cost estimate?
[02:54] Maya: rough ballpark now - about $0.XX per 1k tokens on hosted and lower on dedicated depending on GPU/quantization. we'll put formal numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:05] Priya: on SSO, quick nit: our IdP enforces strict assertion encryption and signed responses, can you support encrypted SAML assertions?
[03:14] Carlos: yes, Redwood supports signed and encrypted assertions; we've integrated with Okta and Azure AD, though sometimes the config needs tweaks (occasionally Saml is typed as 'Sam L' in older docs, sorry).
[03:25] Maya: we'll send the SSO config doc and a sample metadata file.
[03:29] Jon: about audit logs, we want end-to-end traceability from request to model variant used, tokens consumed, and which routing policy served it, is that in the logs?
[03:38] Carlos: yes, logs include request id, route, model version, tokens in/out, and latency. if you want additional fields we can add them to the SIEM forwarder.
[03:47] Priya: retention policy on your side? evidence we can show auditors that we didn't retain full prompt text?
[03:53] Maya: we can provide a data retention spec. by default we retain telemetry for 90 days and redacted prompts unless configured otherwise. we can commit to not storing prompt text for this pilot if needed.
[04:05] Ravi: ok next steps?
[04:07] Maya: Carlos will run initial latency and throughput tests using your sample data; I'll share SOC2/ISO pack and SSO guide; Priya to send RBAC persona list and SIEM field map. we'll reconvene with live bench results.
[04:20] Jon: sounds good.
[04:22] Maya: great thanks all, we'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the benchmark demo.
[04:28] end transcript (auto timestamps approximate; transcription may contain minor errors)
next_steps: Carlos (SE) to run latency/throughput benchmarks on customer sample data (de-identified) and share results by 2029-07-17
Maya (AE) to send SOC 2/ISO artifacts, KMS integration guide, and Okta SAML config doc by 2029-07-11
Priya (Security) to provide RBAC persona list and SIEM field mapping by 2029-07-13
Schedule follow-up demo with live benchmark and role walkthrough on 2029-07-22

Maya Patel: share security pack (SOC 2, ISO summaries) + SSO sample metadata - due 2029-07-11

SSO via Okta (SAML) successfully integrated and tested
KMS integration validated and encryption at rest confirmed
Audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM with required fields and 90-day retention

benchmarks_discussed: Cost: $ per 1k tokens estimates for hosted vs dedicated
Quality: task-specific evals on customer test set (ROUGE-style + manual QA)

notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'KV cash' vs KV cache, 'Sam L' vs SAML). This is a scoping call intended to produce a short pilot (2-4 week bench+validation) focused on security controls and measurable latency/quality targets.
